title: People & Workforce Learnings: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: HR and workforce planning: HR business partners, workforce planners, rostering owners and competence-framework owners
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Draft learnings from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; validate them before adoption.

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's Investigation Status is in_progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person, so this pack stays a draft until the investigation is completed and reviewed.

bottom_line.text: No qualification was defined for the control-room role, so people held emergency duty after a four-day general course.
Rostering had no rule that each shift include a person with practised emergency-isolation competence.
A pressure-boundary repair was manned like routine work: no inspector, no test witness and no close-out reviewer.
The authority to isolate in an emergency sat with senior roles, not with the role that saw the alarm first.
Drill records held no observations, so they could not show whether emergency competence was improving.

items.text: Learnings about systems, not individuals' records.

items.lesson: A safety-critical role needs a defined qualification before anyone is assigned to it.
items.explanation: The enquiry records that the qualification of control-room staff was not defined in HR or operations policy, that new and transferred staff received a four-day general course, and that most staff had attended one basic course since 2018 [EVD-5634]. With no qualification to meet, there was nothing to check before a person took emergency duty. The committee's own benchmark was at least one month of training, preferably on simulators, before control-room duties [EVD-5634].

items.lesson: Recruitment and transfer into the control room had no role-specific standard, so placement rested on availability.
items.explanation: The same four-day general programme served new recruits and transferred staff alike, and the policy set no qualification for the post [EVD-5634]. The findings read this as a selection-and-placement gap, not only a training gap: the night-shift posts were filled from the same broadly trained population [EVD-1460]. The programme risk of staffing a major-hazard control room this way was not assessed.

items.lesson: A known competence gap stays open when no one owns the standard and checks it before rostering.
items.explanation: The training posture for control-room staff was known and accepted: the findings place the gap with operations management and the policy that allowed it [EVD-5634]. No rule tied assignment to emergency duty to a passed assessment, so the gap was carried from 2018 to the night of the release.

items.lesson: Role descriptions must say who may isolate in an emergency, or the decision climbs the hierarchy while the release grows.
items.explanation: The disaster management plan gave no isolation criteria, so the authority to order isolation effectively sat with the most senior shift roles [EVD-4052]. The control-room engineers telephoned the shift in-charges instead of isolating [EVD-1460], and the first isolating valve was closed after the senior officers arrived [EVD-7340].

items.lesson: Authorising a crew for safety-critical maintenance needs a task-level competence standard, not only a job title.
items.explanation: Crews were authorised for pressure-boundary work on the meter without the OEM specification or a test to design pressure [EVD-8645] [EVD-2894], and a calibration crew for the same meter worked without a checklist and left a range change out of the signed record [EVD-2506]. No record shows who authorised the switch to locally bought seals [EVD-8645].

items.lesson: Drill records that hold only dates cannot serve as evidence that emergency competence is being kept up.
items.explanation: Fire drill reports in SAP held no actions or observations, and a separate dataset was kept outside the approved guidelines [EVD-2130]. A competence framework that relies on drills for refresher evidence needs the drill record to capture timings, observations and actions.

rows: Four-day general course; qualification not defined in policy; most staff on one basic course since 2018; no simulator practice
A qualification with simulator emergency scenarios, a pass standard, assessment before rostering and a refresher interval
No isolation criteria in the plan; isolation waited for senior officers
Emergency-command competence, including the delegated authority and criteria to isolate
Work done without the OEM specification and without a test to design pressure
Task authorisation for pressure-boundary work, including the specification check and the pressure test
Range changed and reversed with no checklist and no entry in the signed record
Calibration competence that includes as-found and as-left recording and second-person verification
No such role was assigned to the gasket replacement
Who may act as the independent checker on safety-critical work, and the competence that role needs
Post-incident audit report was one generic page that grouped all nine lamps
Inspection competence for hazardous-area equipment, including recording each item's condition

items.lesson: A roster needs a rule that every shift includes at least one person qualified for the emergency the post may face.
items.explanation: The night-shift control room was held by two engineers drawn from the same four-day-trained population, so neither could compensate for the other [EVD-5634] [EVD-1460]. Both went out to find the leak and were driven back by the cloud [EVD-9220].

items.lesson: Safety-critical maintenance needs to be manned with an independent checker, a test witness and a close-out reviewer, not only the person doing the work.
items.explanation: The 18 September 2020 gasket replacement was resourced with no quality check of the part [EVD-8645], no one to perform or witness a design-pressure test [EVD-2894], and no one to close the notification [EVD-0591]. The only control left was the executing crew's own knowledge.

items.lesson: Critical calibration work needs a second person in the team to verify and record every setting change.
items.explanation: During the December 2019 calibration of the meter, the range was changed from 16000 to 2540 mmwc and back with no mention in the signed records and no checklist [EVD-2506]. No independent verifier was part of the team.

items.text: For `training-designer`: the training needs this pack found are simulator or tabletop scenarios in which access to the source is denied and the crew must isolate from a distance [EVD-5634] [EVD-1460]; the specification check and the test to design pressure for pressure-boundary work [EVD-8645] [EVD-2894]; as-found and as-left recording in calibration [EVD-2506]; and recording observations and actions after each drill [EVD-2130]. This pack sets the standard and the staffing rule; the course content belongs there.

limits: The export holds no evidence on working hours, fatigue or overtime; this pack does not infer fatigue.
F12 is one entity for HR, training and competence in this taxonomy (no F12a/F12b split), so training findings and people-system findings share it; course content is left to training-designer.
The analysis is a desk review of the published enquiry report; it had no access to HR records, rosters or interviews, and it does not review any individual.
